brief: UBS Sales & Trading's weekly Quantitative Conviction screen overlays UBS Quant Research and Systematic Advisory signals onto the stocks where UBS Research and Sales already hold the highest fundamental conviction ahead of earnings, to test where quant indicators agree with that fundamental call and where they diverge. For the week of November 2, the note highlights bullish conviction on PLTR and CVS and cautious conviction on WEIR, WAT, and SARO, from a longer list of US and European names reporting that week. The underlying signals combined into the screen are described with their own backtested track records: hedge fund crowding plus earnings nowcasting (pre-earnings drift, up to +4.3% excess return over 60 days), machine-learning EPS growth forecasts (5.6% annualized, 0.55 Sharpe, beating a 1.5%/0.16-Sharpe consensus-based comparison), hedge fund crowding and crowding momentum (5.3%/0.83 and 6.9%/0.60 annualized), a short-interest-enhanced crowding double-sort, hedge fund-vs-retail positioning (12.2% annualized, 1.07 Sharpe), and hedge fund-vs-mutual-fund positioning (+8.3% US / +5.0% Europe annualized). The note reports these signal histories; it does not argue a single directional thesis beyond the per-stock conviction calls.
